correctness.rationale: C: If k>=2, an occupied singleton with utility zero can move into the gap immediately preceding another occupied run and gain exactly one neighbor, so it is unstable. If a run has length >=3, an interior dissatisfied occupant can profit from a boundary vacancy whenever some vacant run has length >=2. Conversely all dimer occupants already have utility one; with isolated single vacancies, every dissatisfied interior occupied vertex sees two occupied neighbors before moving, and every vacancy continues to have two occupied neighbors after such a move. Counting cyclic gap compositions gives D=n/(k/2)*C(z-1,k/2-1), H=n/z*C(k-z-1,z-1), subtracting the three repeated 110 patterns exactly at k=2z. Independently enumerated literal occupant-to-vacancy jumps for all 2^n bit strings, 3<=n<=12, agreeing with formula at every k, including n=3 and full/empty boundaries. All-n classification follows from run arguments, not finite experiments.
